appliesTo: All cases requiring a suitability report

queries.text: I recommend that you my recommendation is

triggerProbe.presentWhen: The report makes at least one recommendation.

queryGroups.requirement: Client-specific rationale for each recommendation, linked to specified goals

queries.text: I have recommended this because it meets your objective and is in your best interests
this recommendation is suitable for you given your circumstances and what you told me
queries.note: Second wording deliberately targets personalised language for the isClientSpecific judgement.

queries.text: adviser rationale for the recommendation recorded in the file note or planning notes
one recommendation per existing plan retain switch encash advice given
queries.note: Enumerates the discrete recommendations so each can be tested for its own rationale — a report with five actions and one generic rationale block fails this group.

falsePositiveGuards: Identical rationale bullets repeated verbatim across several recommendations are boilerplate — count them once and mark isClientSpecific false.
A rationale that names the client's actual figures, plans or stated words is client-specific even if the sentence structure is templated.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: a recommendation with no stated reason cannot demonstrate suitability.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Note that the rationale is unsupported by any research or meeting record, and weight by how specific the rationale is.

queryGroups.requirement: Justification for the particular product, provider, wrapper and investment

queries.text: why this provider has been recommended platform financial strength service charges
I have recommended a personal pension for the following reasons wrapper choice
why these funds have been selected investment strategy rationale diversification
provider and platform comparison research whole of market panel selection
queries.note: Tests whether the provider rationale is comparative (research-backed) or merely descriptive.

queries.text: centralised investment proposition investment committee approved fund list

falsePositiveGuards: A provider's marketing strengths stated in isolation are not a justification for selecting it over alternatives — distinguish absolute claims from comparative ones.
Firm panel or CIP membership is a legitimate justification if the report says so; do not require a fresh whole-of-market search where a documented panel process exists.

sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Potential Concern where the report asserts a comparison was carried out but no research document exists.

queryGroups.requirement: Personalised language linked to individual circumstances

queries.text: you have told me that you want and this is why the recommendation reflects that
generic explanation of how the product works aims and benefits
queries.note: Deliberately retrieves boilerplate so the ratio of personalised to generic rationale can be judged rather than guessed.

queries.text: specific client preference recorded such as simplicity consolidation adviser involvement

falsePositiveGuards: Standard regulatory wording (tax caveats, past-performance warnings) must be present and is not evidence of impersonal advice.

sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Where personalised claims cite preferences that appear nowhere in the file, treat as unsupported personalisation.

queryGroups.requirement: Alternatives considered and reasons for rejection

queries.text: options considered leave existing plan switch funds internally set up a new plan
I do not recommend this option because reasons for rejection
alternative solutions stakeholder pension considered but not recommended
investment pathways considered and why they are not appropriate for you
queries.note: Required consideration for drawdown cases; frequently appears only as an appendix.

queries.text: comparison of alternative products and providers considered during research
do nothing option leaving things as they are was considered

falsePositiveGuards: Options listed without individual rejection reasons are a partial answer — the check asks for reasons, not just the list.
An alternative rejected in the research file but never mentioned in the report is a report gap, not a research gap.

sufficiency.ifAssertionAbsent: Potential Concern: no alternatives presented to the client.
sufficiency.ifEvidenceAbsent: Where the report claims options were assessed but no research document exists, treat the claim as unsupported.

decision.noIssue: Each discrete recommendation carries its own client-specific rationale naming an objective; product, provider, wrapper and investment choices are justified; and alternatives are presented with reasons for rejection, corroborated by research.
decision.potentialConcern: Rationale is boilerplate or shared verbatim across different recommendations, a recommendation names no objective, provider or wrapper choice is asserted without comparison, or alternatives are absent or listed without reasons.
decision.notApplicable: No recommendation is made in the case.
severityHints: Highest: a recommendation with no rationale at all, or rationale that contradicts the case facts (e.g. 'lower costs' where the charge comparison shows an increase).
High: no alternatives considered on a case where research shows options were compared.
Moderate: rationale present but wholly generic across all recommendations.
Low: an alternative listed with a brief rather than reasoned rejection.
